magnetic fields: Following the Boltzmann distribution and because the energy difference between both states of spin  $1 / 2$  nuclei in a magnetic field is much smaller than the thermal energy, these states are almost equally populated. Consequently, only a tiny population difference effectively contributes to the MR signal- no more than a few ppm per Tesla. As a result, a high concentration of spins is typically required for a high- resolution image, and most MRI scans rely on the ubiquitous and abundant protons of body water (ca.  $10^{2}\mathrm{M}$  to provide the signal.

Nevertheless, the ability to image or spectroscopically analyze species of much lower concentration, such as metabolites in tissues or gases in void spaces, would be enormously powerful for medical practitioners.

Indeed, hyperpolarization can provide the signal enhancement needed to image species of low concentration by enhancing  $P$  by several orders of magnitude.[1] Thus, hyperpolarization holds promise to revolutionize clinical MR imaging and spectroscopy. Hyperpolarization techniques that derive their spin order from parahydrogen  $(\mathrm{pH}_2)$  offer a number of attractive advantages, including very low costs, low instrumentation demands, and rapid high- throughput, and scalable production of hyperpolarized (HP) agents in the liquid state.

Following the Boltzmann distribution, at room temperature  $T\approx 298\mathrm{K}$  all four states are approximately equally populated, thereby resulting in a mixture of  $25\%$ $\mathrm{pH}_2$  and  $75\%$ $\mathrm{OH}_2$  (room- temperature hydrogen,  $\mathrm{rtH}_2$  ).[15] Note that this para fraction  $(f)$  of  $25\%$  does not constitute a particular parahydrogen enrichment, but results from the (almost) equal distribution of all dihydrogen systems in the four available spin states. The apparatus for the production of  $\mathrm{pH}_2$  is composed mainly of three components: an  $\mathrm{H}_2$  source, a low- temperature spin- conversion chamber, and a storage vessel. Most studies have used compressed cylinders as the  $\mathrm{H}_2$  source, but electrolysis is an alternative with beneficial safety properties. When  $\mathrm{H}_2$  is mixed with air at  $4 - 75\%$ $\mathrm{m}\%$  an explosive atmosphere is formed, and so special care must be taken to avoid any accumulation of hydrogen.[16]

$\mathrm{rtH}_2$  is converted into about  $51\%$ $\mathrm{pH}_2$  by flowing the gas through a spin- conversion catalyst at  $77\mathrm{K}$  [17] Alternatively,  $\mathrm{rtH}_2$  can be passed through a catalyst- containing chamber cryogenically chilled to about  $22\mathrm{K}$  to achieve  $>95\%$ $\mathrm{pH}_2$  [16,18] The spin- conversion catalyst is typically made of iron oxides[19] or other metal oxides[20] and is stored in a metal tube,[21] aluminum cylinder,[16b,22] or a glass- trap. The spinconversion catalyst should be completely immersed in the cooling liquid/jacket to avoid back conversion at room temperature. Note that a high  $\mathrm{pH}_2$  enrichment is favorable because the level of hyperpolarization directly depends on it.

Since  $\mathrm{pH}_2$  is in a singlet nuclear state with a combined spin of 0, it does not yield an NMR signal and direct observation by NMR spectroscopy is not possible. However, the para enrichment of a given sample can be determined by NMR spectroscopy by measuring the signal of residual  $\mathrm{OH}_2$  (S(enriched)) which is present in the sample. By comparing S(enriched) to the signal of the same amount of  $\mathrm{H}_2$  in equilibrium at room temperature  $(\mathrm{S}(\mathrm{rtH}_2)$  the para- enrichment fraction  $f$  is obtained [Eq. (1)].[17,22,23]

$$
f = 1 - (3\mathrm{S}(\mathrm{enriched}) / 4\mathrm{S}(\mathrm{rtH}_2)) \tag{1}
$$

For example, the theoretical fraction of  $\mathrm{pH}_2$  enrichment at the temperature of liquid nitrogen is  $51\%$  therefore, the expected ratio of  $\mathrm{S}(\mathrm{rtH}_2) / \mathrm{S}$  (enriched) is 1.53.

The two main variants of hydrogenative PHIP are referred to as PASADENA (parahydrogen and synthesis allow dramatically enhanced nuclear alignment),[2b] where the hydrogenation reaction and NMR detection is carried out entirely at high magnetic field (typically  $>1\mathrm{T}$  and ALTADENA (adiabatic longitudinal transport after dissociation engenders net alignment),[2c] where the hydrogenation reaction is carried out at a low magnetic field (typically  $< 10\mathrm{mT}$  and the hydrogenation product is transferred to a high magnetic field for detection.[25]

This distinction between high and low magnetic fields is based on the homonuclear spin- spin or  $J$  - couplings of the nascent  $\mathrm{pH}_2$  - derived hydrogen atoms in the hydrogenated product: ALTADENA refers to strong, and PASADENA to weak  $J$  coupling regimes.

This distinction between high and low magnetic fields is based on the homonuclear spin- spin or  $J$  - couplings of the nascent  $\mathrm{pH}_2$  - derived hydrogen atoms in the hydrogenated product: ALTADENA refers to strong, and PASADENA to weak  $J$  coupling regimes. A  $J$  - coupling regime is considered weak if the difference in the chemical shifts of the  $\mathrm{pH}_2$  derived protons is much larger than their  $J$  coupling (measured in  $\mathrm{Hz}$  ). Since the chemical shifts depend on the external magnetic field  $(B_0)$  and the  $J$  - couplings do not, choosing an appropriate magnetic field allows the desired  $J$  coupling regime to be realized.

Magnetic field cycling  $(\mathrm{MFC})^{[35]}$  is an alternative method to transfer polarization from nascent  $\mathsf{pH}_2$  derived protons to X nuclei. Here, after the pairwise addition, the static magnetic field is cycled from the Earth's field to nearly zero field and back, in two asymmetrical passages. In other words, isotropic mixing between heteronuclei is achieved and, thanks to the sudden change of the energy levels, the populations of the spin states are rearranged (see Figure 3).

Conversely, the second passage is an adiabatic remagnetization, during which the populations have enough time to adjust to the intermediate Hamiltonians and its eigenstates.[36] "the populations follow the states". Isotropic mixing between heteronuclei is achieved when the frequency difference is the same order of magnitude as their  $J$  - couplings, therefore small scalar couplings require a very low magnetic field (few nT). question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "In general, the basic requirement for hyperpolarization tran..."?
answer: In general, the basic requirement for hyperpolarization transfer is that the symmetry of the two hydrides has to be broken and a coupling between the PTC and substrate spins has to be established.
context:
In general, the basic requirement for hyperpolarization transfer is that the symmetry of the two hydrides has to be broken and a coupling between the PTC and substrate spins has to be established. In many SABRE experiments, there is no difference in the chemical shift of the two hydride spins. In that case, the  $J$ - couplings to the substrate spins break the symmetry and induce magnetic inequivalence, which is the minimum requirement. Specifically, the hydride- substrate  $J$ - couplings through the equatorial plane of the complex (Figure 4) are stronger than  $J$ - couplings through the  $90^{\circ}$  bond at the metal center. This difference is sufficient to induce "spontaneous" spin- order transfer towards the substrate. However, the hyperpolarization transfer strongly depends on the interplay of  $J$ - couplings and resonance frequencies, thus on the magnetic field.

As will be detailed in the following sections, SABRE hyperpolarization is achieved at constant magnetic fields (Section 2.4.2.1), by field cycling (Section 2.4.2.2), or by rf irradiation (Section 2.4.2.3).

There are two main mechanisms that are responsible for "spontaneous" or "continuous"[64] polarization transfer at a constant magnetic field: coherent spin mixing and cross- relaxation.

Coherent spin mixing is usually the dominant mechanism at low magnetic fields, and cross- relaxation[41] prevails at high field.[42] The latter is usually less effective than coherent polarization transfer. However, at high magnetic field, with out the use of rf pulses and magnetic field switching, it can also boost the polarization level by one order of magnitude.[42,43]

Continuous hyperpolarization by coherent spin mixing in a strongly  $J$ - coupled spin system can be understood using the density matrix formalism or, more intuitively, the picture of energy- level anticrossings (LACs; Figure 5).[44] LACs describe a state where the energy levels of the Zeeman eigenstates and the  $J$ - coupling would cross. If there is a coupling between these states, the crossing is avoided, and a "level anticrossing" is formed.[45] At this LAC, mixing between the involved states occurs. This effect can be used to move the population of a given state to a desired state, for example, from the  $\mathsf{pH}_2$  spin order of the hydrides to an observable polarization of the substrate. This leaves room for two different experimental approaches: a) to conduct the experiment at a constant  $B_{\mathrm{LAC}}$  or b) to move the spin system for a given time to  $B_{\mathrm{LAC}}$  and then to a different field for detection. The latter can be achieved by physically cycling the field or by rf irradiation, as described in Sections 2.4.2.2 and 2.4.2.3.

If the experiment is conducted at an LAC, the interesting effect of continuous hyperpolarization is observed. In contrast to the permanent addition of one  $\mathrm{pH}_2$  molecule to one precursor, as discussed in the previous section, the reversible exchange of SABRE allows to repetitively supply  $\mathrm{pH}_2$  spin order. In this way, the hyperpolarization can be continuously renewed and upheld for an extended period of time (e.g. tens of minutes). A constant hyperpolarized magnetization is formed, which recovers after excitation because the agents are re- hyperpolarized by  $\mathrm{pH}_2$ .  $\mathrm{pH}_2$  itself is impervious to rf excitation and depletion, because it has spin 0.

The equilibrium value of the hyperpolarization magnetization is determined by the competing processes of buildup and decay. This effect also allows signal averaging.

(7).[46,49] Such magnetic fields are best established inside  $\mu$ - metal shields that can reduce the surrounding fields more than 1000- fold. Accordingly, this heteronuclear technique was intro duced as SABRE- SHEATH (SABRE in shield enables alignment transfer to heteronuclei), and polarization levels of more than  $34\%$  were reported.[46,50]

In conventional low- field SABRE and in SABRE- SHEATH experiments, polarization transfer proceeds spontaneously as described above, that is, without the application of additional pulse sequences. Similar to in situ PHIP (SAMBADENA and L- PHINEPT+), in situ SABRE hyperpolarization and detection at high field has several advantages. Low- field techniques may be experimentally challenging, requiring a dedicated low- field system or field- cycling setup, followed by sample transfer to take advantage of high- field detection.

Help comes from methods that can be used at high field on any modern and commercially available NMR spectrometer. A basic principle is to use rf fields to produce LAC conditions in the rotating frame as suggested in rf- SABRE,[51] low- irradiation generation of high Tesla- SABRE (LIGHT- SABRE),[52] and rf- SABRE with adiabatic passage through LAC.[53] Unlike a static external magnetic field, the rf field has two adjustable parameters: amplitude and frequency, which can be used as another handle to manipulate the transfer of polarization. For example, it can be utilized to eliminate all the thermally polarized signal (e.g. from  $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ ) to leave only the hyperpolarized signal, which significantly improves the spectral appearance.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "The spin order of  $\mathfrak{p}\mathrm{H}_{2}$  can be tran..."?
answer: The spin order of  $\mathfrak{p}\mathrm{H}_{2}$  can be transformed into the hyperpolarization of protons or heteronuclei provided that the correlation between the nascent proton spins is maintained, that is, the two protons are added to the same substrate molecule in a pairwise manner.
context:
The spin order of  $\mathfrak{p}\mathrm{H}_{2}$  can be transformed into the hyperpolarization of protons or heteronuclei provided that the correlation between the nascent proton spins is maintained, that is, the two protons are added to the same substrate molecule in a pairwise manner. This condition is achieved in the hydrogenation mechanism carried out, for example, by the Wilkinson complex  $\mathrm{(Rh(PPh_3)_3Cl)}$  as well as by the cationic rhodium complexes  $[\mathrm{Rh(diene})\mathrm{L}_2]^+$  (where  $\mathbb{L}$  is a monodentate phosphine) and  $[\mathrm{Rh(diene)diphos}]^+$  (where diphos is a chelating phosphine).[73] The last catalyst, in which the  $\mathrm{Rh}^1$  center is chelated with a bisphosphine ligand, is the most widely employed in PHIP experiments.

The high pairwise efficiency of this catalyst is due to the specific hydrogenation pathway, named the "unsaturate route", in which reversible substrate binding to the metal center is followed by irreversible addition of dihydrogen, which is transferred to the unsaturated substrate through a low- energy activation barrier.[74] This pathway reduces the lifetime of hydrogenation intermediates, during which the singlet state of  $\mathfrak{p}\mathrm{H}_{2}$  may decay (through mixing to the triplet states), and consequently maintains a high efficiency of

hyperpolarization transfer to the product molecule through the addition of a nearly pure singlet state to the multiple bond.[75]
evidence_span: The spin order of  $\mathfrak{p}\mathrm{H}_{2}$  can be transformed into the hyperpolarization of protons or heteronuclei provided that the correlation between the nascent proton spins is maintained, that is, the two protons are added to the same substrate molecule in a pairwise manner.

answer: Biological applications need an aqueous solution of the hyperpolarized product.
context:
Biological applications need an aqueous solution of the hyperpolarized product. Water- soluble catalysts containing water- soluble phosphine ligands have been used.[16a]

However, the toxicity (although being relatively low[76]) of the metal complexes appears to be a limitation to their in vivo application. Filtration of the aqueous solution on a cationic exchange resin allows almost  $90\%$  of the metal complex to be potentially removed, although further investigations are required.[76]

Another method that was proposed to obtain a pure aqueous solution of the hyperpolarizing contrast agent without the metal complex is based on phase separation. Here, a lipophilic precursor of the final, water- soluble, product is hydrogenated in the organic phase. Upon hydrolysis, the agent becomes hydrophilic and can be extracted from the aqueous phase with high purity.[62e,f] This method can be applied to lipophilic precursors, such as anhydrides or esters, and the metal complex is almost completely retained in the organic phase. It also takes advantage of the fact that hydrogenation reactions are often more efficient in organic solvents than in water.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "In the pioneering SABRE experiments, Crabtree's catalyst (an..."?
answer: In the pioneering SABRE experiments, Crabtree's catalyst (an iridium complex with tricyclohexylphosphine and pyridine ligands) and its analogues facilitated the spontaneous polarization transfer from  $\mathrm{pH}_2$  to the exchangeable substrate molecules through rapid substrate and  $\mathrm{H}_2 / \mathrm{pH}_2$  exchange at the Ir center.[38c,d,87] Further developments of the catalytic system by replacement of the phosphine ligand by a carbene ligand drastically increased the efficiency of the polarization transfer.
context:
In the pioneering SABRE experiments, Crabtree's catalyst (an iridium complex with tricyclohexylphosphine and pyridine ligands) and its analogues facilitated the spontaneous polarization transfer from  $\mathrm{pH}_2$  to the exchangeable substrate molecules through rapid substrate and  $\mathrm{H}_2 / \mathrm{pH}_2$  exchange at the Ir center.[38c,d,87] Further developments of the catalytic system by replacement of the phosphine ligand by a carbene ligand drastically increased the efficiency of the polarization transfer. A number of carbene ligands were evaluated.[88]

Although it was clear that "one size may not fit all" substrates, Ir complexes with the 1,3- bis(2,4,6- trimethylphenyl)imidazol- 2- ylidene (IMes) ligand or close derivatives became the "gold standard" of SABRE catalyst because of their stability as well as their broad range of applicability.

Thus, modern catalytic systems for SABRE (Figure 6A) consist of an Ir complex with a) an IMes ligand or its close derivative in one of the axial positions; b) a molecule or nonexchangeable substrate that is permanently attached in the other axial position of the complex during "activation" (hydrogenative removal of diene moiety, Figure 6C); c) exchangeable (to- be- hyperpolarized) substrates, which may or may not be the same as the non- exchangeable substrate in the axial position of the complex.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "Recent developments towards Ir- based heterogeneous catalyst..."?
answer: Recent developments towards Ir- based heterogeneous catalysts have shown promise in terms of separating the contrast agent from the SABRE catalyst as well as the potential for reuse of the catalyst.
context: Recent developments towards Ir- based heterogeneous catalysts have shown promise in terms of separating the contrast agent from the SABRE catalyst as well as the potential for reuse of the catalyst. Shriet al. developed the first immobilized SABRE catalyst based on solid polymer microbeads. The beads were functionalized with 4- dimethylaminopyridine and showed an approximately fivefold enhancement in the  $^{1}\mathrm{H}$  signal of pyridine at  $9.4\mathrm{T}$ .  $^{[97]}$  With the aim of increasing the ratio of the catalyst surface area to volume,  $\mathrm{TiO_2 / PMAA}$  (poly(methacrylic acid)) and PVP (polyvinylpyridine) nanoscale polymer supports were developed with core- shell and "comb" morphologies, respectively.[98] These heterogeneous catalysts yielded approximately 40- fold and 7- fold enhancements, respectively, of the  ${}^{1}\mathrm{H}$  NMR signal of pyridine at  $9.4\mathrm{T}$ ; particle separation and reuse was also demonstrated. More recently, Kovtunov et al. utilized a different synthetic approach to link Ir- based catalyst moieties to  $\mathrm{SiO_2}$  particles functionalized with amine- terminated polymer chains. After bubbling  $\mathrm{pH_2}$  inside a magnetic shield, approximately 100- fold enhancements in the  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  NMR signal (at  $9.4\mathrm{T}$ ) were obtained for  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ - pyridine by SABRE- SHEATH. question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "However, the road to a meaningful in vivo application is ste..."?
answer: However, the road to a meaningful in vivo application is steep.
context:
However, the road to a meaningful in vivo application is steep. Despite the fact that impressive numbers of hyperpolarized agents have led to in vitro signal enhancement, the actual signal- to- noise ratio or resolution in vivo is limited.\[105\] The reason for this is manifold: first, the agent is significantly diluted in blood and tissues, thereby resulting in a label concentration that is much lower than that of water  $(c(^{13}\mathrm{C})< 10^{- 3}\mathrm{M}$  versus  $c(^{1}\mathrm{H})\approx 10^{2}\mathrm{M})$ ; second, the agent needs time to distribute and reach the target; third, the agents may need additional time to cross cell membranes and other organelles before the desired function is probed. During the whole time, relaxation results in a loss of the hyperpolarization at a rate that is faster than that reported in vitro.

Moreover, signal acquisition itself consumes hyperpolarization, because transverse magnetization is required which decays even faster. Currently, no method has achieved the re

hyperpolarization of agents in vivo (although it was proposed[106] and shown in vitro[105b]). Thus, once used up, hyperpolarization magnetization is irrevocably lost and cannot be replenished.
evidence_span: However, the road to a meaningful in vivo application is steep.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "The limited lifetime  $T_{1}$  of magnetic states (often as ..."?
answer: The limited lifetime  $T_{1}$  of magnetic states (often as short as a second or less) significantly reduces the reach and power of hyperpolarization techniques for biomedical imaging.
context: The limited lifetime  $T_{1}$  of magnetic states (often as short as a second or less) significantly reduces the reach and power of hyperpolarization techniques for biomedical imaging. Being based on the  $\mathrm{pH_2}$  singlet, typically represented as  $2^{- 1 / 2}$ $(|\alpha \beta > - |\beta \alpha >)$  , PHIP and SABPE offer the opportunity to generate nuclear spin singlet states with a high efficiency. As a consequence of their symmetry, these states experience much lower relaxation effects in pure solutions,[107] and lifetimes 1- 2 orders of magnitude longer than  $T_{1}$  were reported (up to  $30\mathrm{min}$  for  $\mathrm{^{15}N - ^{15}N}$  singlets and more than an hour for  $^{13}\mathrm{C - ^{13}C}$  singlets).[39e,108] Such lifetimes are, in principle, sufficient for effective biodistribution of the contrast agent before the signal is read out. However, it has been observed that the lifetimes rapidly decrease in aqueous[109] and more viscous media such as physiological fluids.[110] Paramagnetic species such as molecular oxygen[111] or deoxyhemoglobin accelerate the relaxation further.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "The relaxation mechanisms for singlets have been studied and..."?
answer:
The relaxation mechanisms for singlets have been studied and include singlet- triplet leakage, intramolecular dipolar relaxation, symmetric and antisymmetric chemical shift anisotropy (CSA) mechanisms, intermolecular dipolar relaxation, paramagnetic relaxation due to oxygen, and a newly proposed mechanism based on internal motion and coupling of spin with angular momentum, akin to spin rotation (spin- internal motion).[108a,109,111,112]

On the basis of these studies, efforts are underway to identify design criteria for molecules and molecular features that ensure especially long and protected singlet lifetimes.

The water- soluble PHIP contrast agent 2- hydroxyethyl [1-  $^{13}\mathrm{C}]$  - propionate- 2,3,3- d3 (HEP, Figure 7a) was employed in rodents[101b] to track catheter positions, outline the contours of heart and lungs and, in pigs to provide real- time coronary angiography and myocardial perfusion.[113] HEP, which is produced by hydrogenation of the precursor 2- hydroxyethyl  $[1 - ^{13}\mathrm{C}]$  - acrylate]- 2,3,3-  $\mathbb{C}_3$  (HEA), is unlikely to undergo fast metabolic processes. Therefore, Petersson and co- workers[113b- d] made a strong case for employing hyperpolarizing  $^{13}\mathrm{C}$  - HEP for real- time imaging in the cardiovascular system and demonstrated catheter tracking and quantification of myocardial perfusion. context: Succinate (SUC) and NADH generated from the citric acid cycle are oxidized to drive proton- motive force across the inner mitochondrial membrane and ATP synthase. Changes in this fundamental energy pathway have been shown to occur in several disease states which led to the desire to create an imaging agent of the citric acid cycle.  $^{13}$ C- SUC was initially hyperpolarized using the PHIP method from the precursor disodium  $1 - ^{13}\mathrm{C}$  acetylenedicarboxylate (ADC),[8a] which was further optimized by using deuterium labeling (fumaric acid $1 - ^{13}\mathrm{C} - \mathrm{d}_2$ , Figure 7c) to extend the longitudinal relaxation time  $T_{1}$  from 6 to  $27^{\circ}\mathrm{s}$ .[8a] As SUC is a diacid, the  $\mathrm{pH}$  value of the media affects both the  $T_{1}$  and  $J$ - coupling values. The  $J$ - couplings are better resolved in media with a  $\mathrm{pH}$  value far removed from its two  $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$  values, and therefore, PHIP is performed under either basic or acidic conditions. In addition, as a diacid, the ability of hyperpolarized SUC to cross cell membranes is significantly inhibited. To increase the hydrophobicity of the hyperpolarizing contrast agent, the derivative diethyl  $1 - ^{13}\mathrm{C}$ - fumaric acid-  $\mathrm{d}_2$  was developed.[8b] This compound can be hydrogenated and hyperpolarized using a PHIP polarizer with complete conversion into diethyl  $1 - ^{13}\mathrm{C}$ - succinic acid-  $\mathrm{d}_2$  at a final  $\mathrm{pH}$  value after hydrogenation of 6. The  $T_{1}$  value for the compound is  $54\pm 2$  s in a phantom consisting of a 9:1 mixture of water to deuterium oxide. After development of both compounds, the ability of SUC and diethyl succinate (DES) to interrogate metabolism in living systems was explored.

Administration of  $^{13}\mathrm{C - HP}$  TFPP in vivo to atheromatous mice led to increased binding being observed on the endocardial surface of the intact heart compared with normally fed controls.[103] This work demonstrated that TFPP has the potential to act as an in vivo molecular probe for atheromatous plaque imaging and may serve as a model of receptor- targeted bio- imaging with enhanced MR sensitivity. Targeted molecular imaging is an area where HP MRI has not yet been exploited, mostly because the lifetimes of hyperpolarizing contrast agents are typically too short for targeting and clearance. context:
In addition to the previously named contrast agents, many other molecules are under investigation. Most of these contrast agents, however, are somewhat remote from biomedical application.

For example, the hyperpolarization of peptides by SABRE[130] and PHIP[131] techniques has been demonstrated. Although these pioneering studies have reported relatively low polarization levels (i.e.  $P< 1\%$  ), these molecular frameworks are very attractive in the context of potential biomedical applications: for example, for structural biology and as imaging and biocompatible contrast agents.

Considerable research is focused on the hyperpolarization of heteronuclei. For example, despite its relatively short  $T_{1}$  value (i.e. on the order of few seconds),  $^{19}\mathrm{F}$  exhibits attractive properties such as a high MR sensitivity and optimal contrast (a high signal to noise ratio similar to that of protons with no in vivo background signal). Kuhn et al. documented the first studies using monofluorinated styrene and phenylacetylene.[132] Based on these results,  $^{19}\mathrm{F}$  FLASH MRI of hyperpolarized 3- fluorostyrene was carried out by Bommerich et al.[133] In addition to aromatic systems, perfluorinated octane and octene were examined by Plaumann et al.[134] These molecules have a structure analogous to perflubron, which was already used as a contrast agent.[135] Signal enhancements were utilized for  $^{19}\mathrm{F}$  MRI.[134]

Nicotinamide (vitaminB3 amide) was hyperpolarized through SABRE in 2009. [38a] Following this pioneering study, the hyperpolarization of aqueous nicotinamide solutions was shown,[91a] thus paving the way for the potential preparation of biologically compatible formulations.

Moreover, efficient  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  hyperpolarization  $(\% P_{15\mathrm{N}}\approx 7-$ $10\%$  by SABRE- SHEATH)[46,91b] has been demonstrated, and an efficient synthesis of the  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  - enriched (ca.  $98\%$  ) biomolecule has been developed.[91b] Hyperpolarization of  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  is desirable due to the significantly longer lifetime of  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  sites compared to that of protons.[39d,e] Nicotinamide can be administered in high dose (up to  $8\mathrm{g}$  in humans[142]), and the ubiquitous role of this vitamin in metabolism means that various bio- imaging applications are possible. For example, the imaging of the action/efficacy of nicotinamide phosphoribosyl transferase (NAMPT) inhibitors[143] in cancer treatment can be envisioned,[144] because some cancer cells may be

extremely sensitive to these inhibitors, which block the metabolism of nicotinamide, and result in death of the cancer cells.[145]

In the context of biomedical imaging applications,  $\mathrm{pH}_{2}$ - based hyperpolarization techniques still have a long way to go to mature to the same state of technology as SEOP as well as dissolution DNP contrast agents and their production. Currently,  $\mathrm{pH}_{2}$  generators are commercially available, but there are no automated commercial hyperpolarizers for the production of  $\mathrm{pH}_{2}$ - based contrast agents for sale. The past several years have certainly seen a renaissance in  $\mathrm{pH}_{2}$ - based polarizers and spin physics.

Fundamentally, the cost of PHIP and SABRE hyperpolarization equipment (excluding the  $\mathrm{pH}_{2}$  generator) is relatively low ( $\ll 10^5 \in$  and it is our hope that commercially available PHIP and SABRE equipment for the production of hyperpolarizing contrast agents will soon emerge. The cost of  $\mathrm{pH}_{2}$  generators varies from about  $10^5 \in$  for liquid nitrogen setups to about  $10^5 \in$  for cryogenically cooled devices; however, because of its long lifetime, the shipping of  $\mathrm{pH}_{2}$  appears feasible, such that one generator may cater a larger community.

Although these solutions don't exhibit significant toxicity, and can be used for animal studies, the development of catalyst- free formulations for injection remains a top priority and an active area of research.

However, the preparation of highly polarized ( $P > 10\%$ ) and highly concentrated (i.e.  $>20 \mathrm{mM}$ , preferably  $>100 \mathrm{mM}$ ) aqueous solutions has not yet been demonstrated.

Peter J. Rayner and Simon B. Duckett*

Signal amplification by reversible exchange (SABRE) turns typically weak magnetic resonance responses into strong signals making previously impractical measurements possible. This technique has gained significant popularity because of its speed and simplicity. This Minireview tracks the development of SABRE from the initial hyperpolarization of pyridine in 2009 to the point in which  $50\%$ $^1 H$  polarization levels have been achieved in a di- deuterio- nicotinate, a key step in the pathway to potential clinical use. Simple routes to highly efficient  $^{15}N$  hyperpolarization and the creation of hyperpolarized long- lived magnetic states are illustrated. To conclude, we describe how the recently reported SABRE- RELAY approach offers a route for parahydrogen to hyperpolarize a much wider array of molecular scaffolds, such as amides, alcohols, carboxylic acids, and phosphates, than was previously thought possible. We predict that collectively these developments ensure that SABRE will significantly impact on both chemical analysis and the diagnosis of disease in the future.

answer: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are now ubiquitous techniques that are used in the study of molecules and materials despite an inherent insensitivity.
context: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are now ubiquitous techniques that are used in the study of molecules and materials despite an inherent insensitivity. Classically, the small Boltzmann- derived spin energy level population difference is overcome through the use of large magnetic fields, increased sample concentrations, and extended signal averaging. However, these approaches have both time and cost implications, and for this reason, essentially all current clinical MRI applications make use of a water signal because of its high in vivo concentration. Thus, hyperpolarization methods that create a non- Boltzmann population distribution of magnetic spins are highly desirable and have now begun to influence biomedical imaging and disease diagnosis.[1] Spin- exchange optical pumping (SEOP) and dynamic nuclear hyperpolarization (DNP) are two of the most clinically developed approaches, having been successfully used for the study of lung physiology and prostate cancer metabolomics, respectively.[1c,d,2] Hence, hyperpolarized MRI is predicted to play a growing role in human health.[1a,3]

In addition, given the widespread use of NMR spectroscopy for the characterization of materials in solution, hyperpolarization also opens up potential routes for analysis in which only small amounts of analyte are available.[4] Such methods are likely to be of great importance for the detection and identification of trace impurities in the pharmaceutical pipeline. Furthermore, the identification of transient reaction intermediates involved in catalytic processes reflect a further area in which hyperpolarization studies might be expected to aid the improvement of reaction outcomes and, thus, reduce the environmental impact of industrial processes.[5]

An alternative and simple route to nuclear spin polarization involves the addition of singlet- state- based parahydrogen  $(p - \mathrm{H}_2)$  to an unsaturated center, collectively termed parahydrogen- induced polarization (PHIP).[6] The potential clinical uptake of PHIP techniques has been hindered by the need for a chemical change—commonly hydrogenation of organic molecules such as alkynes and alkenes—which limits the range of suitable substrates.[7] Recently, the use of cleavable, unsaturated molecular tags, including propargyl esters, has broadened the scope of the PHIP method to include access to pyruvate, acetate, and even lactate for the monitoring of metabolism in vitro.[8]

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "The SABRE phenomenon was originally described using a densit..."?
answer: The SABRE phenomenon was originally described using a density matrix theory approach based on a model four- spin system derived from two spins that originate in  $p\text{- }\mathrm{H}_{2}$  and two that originate in the bound substrate.[10] The low field evolution of the polarization as a function of magnetic field was modelled, and the effect of transport into the magnet considered.

The analytical solution predicts that scalar coupling in the SABRE catalyst results in the transfer of spin order between the  $p\text{- }\mathrm{H}_{2}$  - derived hydride ligands and the two additional bound nuclei. These nuclei were found to retain enhanced populations of visible longitudinal single spin (the normal Zeeman polarization) and two- spin order terms after substrate dissociation. However, the associated zero quantum terms were stated to reflect the creation of singlet states that would be preserved in ultra- low field. Unfortunately, while being accurate, this model's reliability depends critically on several very small  $J$  - couplings that are hard to measure.

answer: A complementary method based on level anti- crossings (LACs) yields analogous but more qualitative results, whilst providing a much clearer and intuitive picture of the origin of SABRE polarization.[11,13a] A LAC arises at a magnetic field where two energy levels would cross in the absence of spinspin coupling.
context: A complementary method based on level anti- crossings (LACs) yields analogous but more qualitative results, whilst providing a much clearer and intuitive picture of the origin of SABRE polarization.[11,13a] A LAC arises at a magnetic field where two energy levels would cross in the absence of spinspin coupling. For SABRE, efficient mixing of the corresponding substrate and  $p\text{- }\mathrm{H}_{2}$  derived spin- states therefore occurs when substrate and hydride resonance frequency differences match the difference between the mutual hydride spin couplings and the sum of one quarter of their mutual couplings to substrate.[13c] Hence, spin order transfer efficien cy depends explicitly on the scalar coupling network within the catalyst and the magnetic field experienced at the point of polarization transfer. Thus, this method has the benefit of enabling the rapid prediction of the optimum magnetization transfer field for a particular substrate.

However, as SABRE is a dynamic process, the effect of chemical exchange of  $p\text{- }\mathrm{H}_{2}$  and the substrate at the catalyst need to be considered. Furthermore, spin state relaxation during this process tempers the buildup of SABRE- derived polarization in solution. An analytical model that combines kinetics and nuclear spin evolution has been presented that addresses these concerns.[13b] This model predicted that optimal SABRE transfer, in the low- field regime, occurs when the rate constant for substrate dissociation is on the order of the spin mixing frequency at a LAC. Conversely, the substrate dissociation rates should be as fast as possible for high- field SABRE. Additionally, the relative concentrations of  $p\text{- }\mathrm{H}_{2}$  substrate, and catalyst are important, with large signal enhancements resulting for low substrate- to- catalyst ratios and high  $p\text{- }\mathrm{H}_{2}$  - to- catalyst ratios. The authors conclude that relaxation within the active catalyst can inhibit efficient polarization buildup.

Both the steady- state and dynamic behavior of the SABRE process have been considered using a strategy that takes into account spin evolution in the catalyst and substrate exchange.[13c] This method allows for multi- spin systems, timedependent SABRE polarization and polarization formed through r.f. irradiation. This report also includes a comparison of the theoretical descriptions of the SABRE effect.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "Polarization can also be transferred to heteronuclei bound d..."?
answer: Polarization can also be transferred to heteronuclei bound directly to the catalyst through a  $^2 J_{\mathrm{HX}}$  scalar coupling.
context:
Polarization can also be transferred to heteronuclei bound directly to the catalyst through a  $^2 J_{\mathrm{HX}}$  scalar coupling. This refinement has been exemplified for both  ${}^{15}\mathrm{N}$  [27] and  ${}^{31}\mathrm{P}$  [28] hyperpolarization. When a  $^2 J_{\mathrm{HX}}$  scalar coupling is used, the optimum transfer field can now be in the region of approximately  $0.2 - 0.4\mu \mathrm{T}$  which is achieved by conducting the SABRE catalysis inside a  $\mu$  - magnetic shield.[27a] This protocol has been termed SABRE- SHEATH (signal amplification by reversible exchange- in shield enables alignment transfer to heteronuclei) and its scope is discussed in detail in Sections 4 and 5.

A drawback of conducting the SABRE polarization transfer in low magnetic fields is the requirement for fast transfer into high field in which detection takes place. Alternate approaches use radio frequency (r.f.) methods to transfer polarization at high field within the observation magnet. Thus, immediate detection and recycling is possible, which provides a simple route to rapid repetitive measurements.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "As discussed, in order for  $p\mathrm{- H}_2$  to be harness..."?
answer: As discussed, in order for  $p\mathrm{- H}_2$  to be harnessed, its symmetry must be broken.
context: As discussed, in order for  $p\mathrm{- H}_2$  to be harnessed, its symmetry must be broken. High- symmetry SABRE catalysts of the type  $[\mathrm{Ir(H)}_2(\mathrm{IMes})(\mathrm{substrate})_3]^+$  actually rely upon magnetic inequivalence for polarization transfer. However, by adding a coligand it is possible to form complexes of type  $[\mathrm{Ir(H)}_2(\mathrm{IMes})(\mathrm{substrate})_3(\mathrm{coligand})]^+$ . In this scenario, the hydride ligands are chemically distinct and polarization transfer results from both coupling and chemical shift asymmetry. The strength of the hydride- hydride and hydride- substrate couplings and catalyst lifetimes can again be changed by varying the identity of the catalyst and consequently tunable hyperpolarization efficiency is achieved, although in this case polarization transfer into the axial ligands can occur. A number of examples have utilized an equatorially bound coligand, such as acetonitrile, to break the chemical symmetry of the SABRE active catalysis.[20,23b,32] In this case, both acetonitrile and the target substrate are hyperpolarized. An alternative approach utilized a fully deuterated isotopologue of the targeted SABRE substrate as a coligand.[25,32,33] In this case, the coligand does not receive visible polarization itself and has the effect of focusing the polarization into the  ${}^{1}\mathrm{H}$  sites on the target substrate. This method has yielded almost double the polarization level that could be achieved in the absence of the coligand.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "A well- established route to improve the efficacy of hyperpo..."?
answer: A well- established route to improve the efficacy of hyperpolarization techniques is the selective deuteration of the substrate.
context:
A well- established route to improve the efficacy of hyperpolarization techniques is the selective deuteration of the substrate. $^{[42]}$  When applied to the SABRE technique,  $3,4,5 - d_{3}$ - pyridine showed improved performance over its protio analogue. $^{[17,43]}$  A detailed study that probed the optimal deuteration pattern has been reported for nicotinamide and methyl nicotinate. $^{[33]}$  Placement of a proton ortho to the nitrogen binding site was shown to be optimal for efficient polarization transfer but coupling to a remote proton was optimal for a long magnetic state lifetime. Similar improvements have now also been reported for the tuberculosis drug isoniazid and its derivatives. $^{[35]}$

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "SABRE harnesses the long- lived singlet state of  $p\mathrm{..."?
answer: SABRE harnesses the long- lived singlet state of  $p\mathrm{- H}_2$  as its source of polarization.
context:
SABRE harnesses the long- lived singlet state of  $p\mathrm{- H}_2$  as its source of polarization. In this context, singlet states are non- magnetic spin isomers of a coupled spin- 1/2 pair, which are immune to external dipolar coupling. It is therefore possible to identify other molecules in which two almost identical protons exist in a singlet state. $^{[44]}$  The SABRE technique can hyperpolarize such states, as was exemplified for the strongly coupled  ${}^{1}\mathrm{H}$ - pair in 2- aminothiazole $^{[45]}$  in which the singlet state was accessed in  $90\%$  efficiency by r.f. methods and using a spin- lock as pioneered by Levitt. $^{[44]}$  This approach has also been applied to derivatives of nicotinamide and pyrazinamide that have isolated spin- pairs through selective deuteration. $^{[46]}$

The current state of the art utilizes a pyridazine- based  ${}^{1}\mathrm{H}$ - spin pair that exhibit a  $\Delta \delta$  of only  $1\mathrm{Hz}$  despite having a strong  ${}^{3}J_{\mathrm{HH}}$  coupling. $^{[47]}$  As a consequence the state lifetime was observed to be over  $4\mathrm{min}$  at low field and a SABRE hyperpolarized signal could still be observed  $15\mathrm{min}$  after polarization transfer. This method shows great potential for progression towards clinical applications as the polarization can be stored in long- lived singlet state prior to injection and then subsequently observed in vivo.
evidence_span: SABRE harnesses the long- lived singlet state of  $p\mathrm{- H}_2$  as its source of polarization.

SABRE- induced hyperpolarization of  ${}^{31}\mathrm{P}$  nuclei was also shown for a range of phosphorus- substituted  $N$ - heterocycles in which up to a 3588- fold enhancement at  $9.4\mathrm{T}$  resulted.[58] This example involved indirect transfer to  ${}^{31}\mathrm{P}$  through  ${}^{1}\mathrm{H}$  nuclei on the pyridyl ring with the optimum PTF being  $45\mathrm{G}$  and could be conducted at room temperature. question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "The SABRE- induced hyperpolarization of  ${}^{19}\mathrm{F}$..."?
answer: The SABRE- induced hyperpolarization of  ${}^{19}\mathrm{F}$  nuclei was initially reported for 3- fluoropyridine in 2009 though enhancement factors were not quoted.[59] More recently the polarization of 3- fluoropyridine was revisited with a view to developing  ${}^{19}\mathrm{F}$  molecular imaging probes.[59] In this report, polarization levels of up to circa  $0.28\%$  (93- fold enhancement at  $9.4\mathrm{T}$ ) were observed.

On addition of concentrated  $\mathrm{HC}_{\mathrm{(aq)}}$  to the solution, a  $10\mathrm{ppm}$ ${}^{19}\mathrm{F}$  chemical shift difference was reported, however, the enhancement was reduced to 13- fold because of extended sample handling times. Despite potential benefits for biomedical translation of  ${}^{19}\mathrm{F}$  molecular imaging, such as using the  ${}^{1}\mathrm{H}$ - channel on existing hospital MRI scanners and no biological background signal, the  ${}^{19}\mathrm{F}$  nucleus in 3- fluoropyridine has a  $T_{1}$  value of just  $10.3\mathrm{s}$  at  $9.4\mathrm{T}$  and therefore perhaps precludes its use for in vivo imaging techniques. This highlights the need for the development of novel  ${}^{19}\mathrm{F}$  contrast agents with extended lifetimes.

It is particularly advantageous for investigating analytes that are in low concentrations in solution.[4e,61] For example, a solution containing just  $2\mu \mathrm{mol}$  of quinoline was hyperpolarized using SABRE in an automated flow system, which allowed for the collection of  ${}^{13}\mathrm{C}$ ,  ${}^{1}\mathrm{H}$ , and NOE data in addition to the 2D techniques, COSY and HMBC.[61] SABRE can also be used to acquire 2D spectra utilizing FAST- NMR methods.[62] This has led to ultrafast COSY being recorded in under  ${}^{1}\mathrm{s}$ .[61]

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "A limitation of low- concentration measurements is that the ..."?
answer: A limitation of low- concentration measurements is that the active SABRE catalyst typically requires three substrate molecules to bind to the iridium center.
context: A limitation of low- concentration measurements is that the active SABRE catalyst typically requires three substrate molecules to bind to the iridium center. Therefore, at substoichiometric amounts of substrate, the SABRE effect is prohibited. To overcome this, it is possible to use 1- methyl- 1,2,3- triazole as a co- ligand to stabilize the catalyst.[4e] Importantly, it was noted that at substoichiometric substrate levels there was a linear relationship between substrate concentration and signal enhancement. This phenomenon has been exploited for the quantitative analysis of complex mixtures in single- scan SABRE- polarized  ${}^{1}\mathrm{H}$  NMR spectra.[63] These techniques have been applied to the study of analytes within biofluids[4d] and could allow for wider detection of drug metabolites in urine samples in the future. Low- concentration analytes have also been detected by utilizing continuous SABRE hyperpolarization at high magnetic fields.[4f] More recently, Reile et al. have described the resolution of six dilute analytes by SABRE hyperpolarization coupled with diffusion ordered spectroscopy (DOSY).[64]
evidence_span: A limitation of low- concentration measurements is that the active SABRE catalyst typically requires three substrate molecules to bind to the iridium center.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "Heterogeneous SABRE also reflects a potential route to creat..."?
answer: Heterogeneous SABRE also reflects a potential route to create a biocompatible bolus as the catalyst could be easily removed.
context:
Heterogeneous SABRE also reflects a potential route to create a biocompatible bolus as the catalyst could be easily removed. Heterogeneous catalysis has been widely applied in PHIP and DNP methods previously.[71] For SABRE, the immobilized iridium- NHC catalyst on polymer microbeads (8) gave circa 5- fold  ${ }^{1} \mathrm{H}$ - enhancement at  $9.4 \mathrm{~T}$  for the ortho-

protons of pyridine (Figure 8).[72] This enhancement, despite being low, was shown to be achieved only from the heterogeneous catalysis by comparison to control experiments on the supernatant solution. Alternatively, an iridium- NHC catalyst immobilized on silica gel (9) led to a 100- fold  ${ }^{15} \mathrm{~N}$ - enhancement at  $9.4 \mathrm{~T}$  in  ${ }^{15} \mathrm{~N}$ - pyridine after polarization transfer at low magnetic fields in methanol.[73]

Figure 8. Heterogeneous SABRE catalysts. Reproduced with permission from Refs. [72,73].

Currently, neither heterogeneous SABRE nor aqueous SABRE delivers polarization levels that are commensurate with biomedical imaging. Additionally, the heterogeneous catalysis has only been reported in methanol solutions, which are not biocompatible, and thus further development is required before this high potential technique can be realized for in vivo applications.
evidence_span: Heterogeneous SABRE also reflects a potential route to create a biocompatible bolus as the catalyst could be easily removed.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "A facile route to produce a potentially biocompatible bolus ..."?
answer: A facile route to produce a potentially biocompatible bolus for in vivo investigation has been reported through the use of biphasic catalysis (Figure 9).
context:
A facile route to produce a potentially biocompatible bolus for in vivo investigation has been reported through the use of biphasic catalysis (Figure 9). This allows the catalyst to remain in the organic phase, and the aqueous phase, containing the hyperpolarized substrate, can be separated as previously established for PHIP.[8,71f] Biphasic SABRE catalysis, dubbed catalyst- separated hyperpolarization via signal amplification by reversible exchange (CASH- SABRE), has been exemplified using  $0.3 \mathrm{~mL}$  of  $\mathrm{CDCl}_{3}$  containing  $5 \mathrm{~mM}$  of  $\left[\mathrm{IrCl}(\mathrm{COD})(\mathrm{IMes})\right]$  and  $0.3 \mathrm{~mL}$  of  $\mathrm{D}_{2} \mathrm{O}$  containing  $20 - 100 \mathrm{~mM}$  of the hyperpolarization target and  $0.16 \mathrm{~w} / \mathrm{v} \% \mathrm{NaCl}$ .[74] This led to up to 3000- fold signal enhancement at  $9.4 \mathrm{~T}$  when using methyl  $4,6 - d_{2}$ - nicotinate. Importantly, just  $1.5 \times 10^{- 6} \mathrm{~M}$  of the iridium catalyst and  $0.06 \% \mathrm{CDCl}_{3}$  contamination in the aqueous phase was observed. This method has been exemplified with a number of substrates, and images

Figure 9. Schematic of biphasic SABRE catalysis.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "In summary, SABRE is a simple hyperpolarization technique th..."?
answer: In summary, SABRE is a simple hyperpolarization technique that brings together many different approaches of magnetic resonance, synthetic chemistry, and catalysis.
context:
In summary, SABRE is a simple hyperpolarization technique that brings together many different approaches of magnetic resonance, synthetic chemistry, and catalysis. There is a need to understand all of these components if very high polarization levels are to be achieved more generally. At the heart of the SABRE process is the metal catalyst that mediates polarization transfer, and modification of the catalyst has caused significant improvements in SABRE efficacy. This polarization technique has been applied to a range of nuclei and has begun to improve a number of analytical methods. The key breakthrough for application of the SABRE technique in a clinical setting will be the observation of a polarized substrate in vivo and this could open the door to studying disease models in real time.

Finally, whilst it is established that  ${}^{1}\mathrm{H}$  and spin-  $\cdot 1 / 2$  heteronuclei can be readily sensitized by SABRE, the range of molecules is limited by the necessity to bind to the metal center; only aromatic heterocycles, nitriles, Schiff bases, and diazirines currently feature regularly. Thus, harnessing  $p\mathrm{- H}_2$  more widely will be the key to the future development of SABRE, particularly with the proven use of pyruvate, glucose, and urea in in vivo DNP studies.
evidence_span: In summary, SABRE is a simple hyperpolarization technique that brings together many different approaches of magnetic resonance, synthetic chemistry, and catalysis.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "Overcoming the requirement for binding the target substrate ..."?
answer: Overcoming the requirement for binding the target substrate to the metal catalyst has recently been achieved using a technique that has been named SABRE- RELAY.[75] This method begins by using SABRE to hyperpolarize an amine or ammonia, and proton exchanges allow the relay of polarization into the target substrate (Scheme 2).
context:
Overcoming the requirement for binding the target substrate to the metal catalyst has recently been achieved using a technique that has been named SABRE- RELAY.[75] This method begins by using SABRE to hyperpolarize an amine or ammonia, and proton exchanges allow the relay of polarization into the target substrate (Scheme 2).  ${}^{1}\mathrm{H}$  NMR signal gains of up to 650- fold per proton were reported in conjunction with  ${}^{13}\mathrm{C}$  signal enhancements at  $9.4\mathrm{T}$  of 570- fold for 1- propanol. Importantly, the simple polarization of  ${}^{1}\mathrm{H}$ ,  ${}^{13}\mathrm{C}$ ,  ${}^{31}\mathrm{P}$ , and  ${}^{15}\mathrm{N}$  nuclei in a range of amide, alcohol, carboxylic acid, phosphate, and carbonate substrates was exemplified. Moreover, as this methodology gives access to hyperpolarized pyruvate, glucose, and urea, it may, with development, ultimately reflect a cost efficient alternative to DNP. We predict that the advent of SABRE- RELAY will greatly increase the range of  $p\mathrm{- H}_2$ - based hyperpolarization applications in the future and encourage a far greater array of researchers to contribute to these developments.

Scheme 2. Schematic of the SABRE-RELAY process in which an amine or ammonia is polarized and then subsequently relays its polarization to a target substrate (sub) by proton exchange.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "Amino acids (AAs) and ammonia are metabolic markers essentia..."?
answer: Amino acids (AAs) and ammonia are metabolic markers essential for nitrogen metabolism and cell regulation in both plants and humans.
context: Amino acids (AAs) and ammonia are metabolic markers essential for nitrogen metabolism and cell regulation in both plants and humans. NMR provides interesting opportunities to investigate these metabolic pathways, yet lacks sensitivity, especially in case of  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ . In this study, spin order embedded in  $\mathsf{p} - \mathsf{H}_2$  is used to produce on- demand reversible hyperpolarization in  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  of pristine alanine and ammonia under ambient protic conditions directly in the NMR spectrometer. This is made possible by designing a mixed- ligand Ir- catalyst, selectively ligating the amino group of AA by exploiting ammonia as a strongly competitive co- ligand and preventing deactivation of Ir by bidentate ligation of AA. The stereoisomerism of the catalyst complexes is determined by hydride fingerprinting using  $^{1}\mathrm{H} / \mathrm{D}$  scrambling of the associated N- functional groups on the catalyst (i.e., isotopological fingerprinting), and unravelled by 2D- ZQ- NMR. Monitoring the transfer of spin order from  $\mathsf{p} - \mathsf{H}_2$  to  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  nuclei of ligated and free alanine and ammonia targets using SABRE- INEPT with variable exchange delays pinpoints the monodentate elucidated catalyst complexes to be most SABRE active. Also RF- spin locking (SABRE- SLIC) enables transfer of hyperpolarization to  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ . The presented high- field approach can be a valuable alternative to SABRE- SHEATH techniques since the obtained catalytic insights (stereochemistry and kinetics) will remain valid at ultra- low magnetic fields.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "The concept of nuclear spin hyperpolarization is a very attr..."?
answer: The concept of nuclear spin hyperpolarization is a very attractive route to push NMR beyond its current boundaries.[11,17- 22] Numerous research endeavors spanning more than half a century have resulted in a wide array of physically and/or chemically orientated hyperpolarization strategies, each with its benefits and pitfalls.[23- 28] Sensitivity enhancement is often considered the main factor for choosing a hyperpolarization strategy.
context:
The concept of nuclear spin hyperpolarization is a very attractive route to push NMR beyond its current boundaries.[11,17- 22] Numerous research endeavors spanning more than half a century have resulted in a wide array of physically and/or chemically orientated hyperpolarization strategies, each with its benefits and pitfalls.[23- 28] Sensitivity enhancement is often considered the main factor for choosing a hyperpolarization strategy. But in reality, the practicality of using it under experimental conditions can even be more important for the future development of hyperpolarization applications in academia and industry.[29,30]

In this regard, parahydrogen  $(\mathrm{p - H}_2)$ , the singlet spin isomer of molecular hydrogen, stands out as a cost- effective and efficient hyperpolarization agent for enhancing spin order into interesting nuclei such as  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ .[31- 34]  $\mathrm{P - H}_2$  can be produced cost- effectively on demand,[35] can provide a fast hyperpolarization build- up time in seconds,[36] and can be deployed under ambient experimental conditions.[37] Using transition metal catalysis,  $\mathrm{p - H}_2$  s undetectable singlet magnetization is unlocked.[38,39] After being unlocked, the spin order can then be directed toward heteronuclear spins like  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ , which have slow signal relaxation, resulting in a prolonged sensitivity boost for hyperpolarized targets in solution.[36,40- 43]

NMR studies involving AAs and/or ammonia can benefit immensely from this  $\mathrm{p - H}_2$  - enhanced sensitivity gain.[33,34,44] Specifically in the case of AAs, various elegant methodologies using hydrogenative parahydrogen- induced polarization (PHIP) have been proposed, yet with one common shortcoming: initial chemical modification of the AA is required, making the technology less broadly applicable.[45- 47] PHIP- label and PHIP side arm hydrogenation (PHIP- SAH) rely on unsaturated carbon- carbon side groups functionalized onto the AA. Pairwise hydrogenation with  $\mathrm{p - H}_2$ , possibly followed by cleavage of their side- arm group, redistributes hyperpolarization across the AA.[45,48- 50]

It has thus become a quest to find an alternative for hyperpolarization of unmodified AAs.[33] Application of the signal amplification by reversible exchange (SABRE) strategy instantly comes to mind.[51,52] SABRE relies on reversible spin transfer catalysis, maintaining a balance between i) coherent spin physics involving  $\mathrm{p - H}_2$  on the active catalyst and ii) reversible chemical (ligand) exchange of the molecular target on and off the active catalyst. However, in the case of AAs, strong bidentate chelation of the metal center by the AA disrupts this balance (Figure 1a) and makes hyperpolarization with SABRE exceptionally challenging.[33,53,54,34]

At equilibrium, the relative concentrations of the different isotopologues are described by a binomial distribution (Equation (1)):

$$

$$

answer: In the octahedral SABRE complex, ZQ coherences created from the longitudinal triplet magnetization of a hydride couple evolve under their chemical shift difference.[61] Such chemical shift difference is generated when different ligands or different isotopologues of the same ligand occupy the equatorial positions (trans to the hydrides).
context: In the octahedral SABRE complex, ZQ coherences created from the longitudinal triplet magnetization of a hydride couple evolve under their chemical shift difference.[61] Such chemical shift difference is generated when different ligands or different isotopologues of the same ligand occupy the equatorial positions (trans to the hydrides). Consequently, the rate of ZQ evolution becomes dependent on the chemical and isotopological composition of the complex (Figure 4b). Plotting the ZQ evolution rate of the hydrides versus their chemical shift in a 2D ZQ plot readily separates out the hydride couples for each unique structure. This approach also provides an isotopological fingerprint assisting to discriminate all substrates (ammonia and/or alanine) bound in each complex.[54,61] A detailed description of the pulse sequence and experimental conditions allowing the construction of such 2D ZQ plots is provided in the experimental procedure details available in the Supporting Information (Figures S3, S6, S12, Supporting Information).

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "In contrast to equatorial ligands, axial ligands only exert ..."?
answer: In contrast to equatorial ligands, axial ligands only exert minimal influence on the hydrides situated in the equatorial plane.
context: In contrast to equatorial ligands, axial ligands only exert minimal influence on the hydrides situated in the equatorial plane. Isotopological scrambling in the axial position did not seem to affect the equatorially positioned hydrides. The association of different functional groups in the axial position has however been shown to induce a chemical shift translation of equatorial motifs. This effect has been ascribed to both steric and electronic effects.[61,73] Figure 4a reveals two separated hydride regions, hinting at the presence of different ligands in the axial positions of the complexes associated with motifs I- IV (from  $\delta - 23.45$  to  $- 24.00\mathrm{ppm}$ ) and motifs V- VI (from  $\delta - 22.35$  to  $- 22.65\mathrm{ppm}$ ). The chemical shift range from  $\delta - 23.45$  to  $- 24.00\mathrm{ppm}$  shows the hydride couple fingerprints of complexes with nitrogen functional groups in their axial positions (vide infra).[32,61] In the present system, the hydride resonances occurring in this region are associated with complexes containing either ammonia or N- bonded alanine in their axial position. The chemical shift range from  $\delta - 22.35$  to  $- 22.65\mathrm{ppm}$  in Figure 4a shows fingerprints of complexes with oxygen functional groups in their axial positions (vide infra).

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "Motifs III- IVThe catalyst configurations corresponding to m..."?
answer: Motifs III- IVThe catalyst configurations corresponding to motifs III to IV were analyzed in detail based on the ZQ- plot shown in Figure 4a, again combined with 1D spectra acquired on catalysts mixtures containing either  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ - labelled ammonia or  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ - labelled alanine (Figure 4c).
context: 2.4.2. Motifs III- IVThe catalyst configurations corresponding to motifs III to IV were analyzed in detail based on the ZQ- plot shown in Figure 4a, again combined with 1D spectra acquired on catalysts mixtures containing either  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ - labelled ammonia or  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ - labelled alanine (Figure 4c). Motif III (Figure 4a, dark blue) and motif IV (Figure 4a, light blue) represent two complexes containing both ammonia and N- bonded alanine in their equatorial plane. As highlighted in the zoomed- in version of motif IV in Figure 4b, the left side of motifs III and IV, marked with  $\mathrm{H}'$ , shows a  $3 \times 2$  pattern. At the  $^{1}\mathrm{H} / \mathrm{D}$  ratio in the system, this isotopological distribution in combination with its chemical shift reveals a hydride positioned trans to ammonia. The corresponding right- shifted hydride resonances belonging to complexes III and IV, marked with  $\mathrm{H}$  in Figure 4a, are split twofold, yielding a  $2 \times 3$  motif. Following the method discussed in Vaneeckhaute et al.,[61] this pattern can be assigned to a hydride trans to a primary amine. Note that the  $^{1}\mathrm{H}$  content of the system only allows for partial isotopological scrambling. Fully isotopological scrambled fingerprints for a hydride trans to ammonia and a primary amine should respectively result in a  $4 \times 3$  and  $3 \times 4$  motif. However, for the quantity of protons used in our chemical system (see Figure S4, Supporting Information), the concentration of the fully protonated isotopologues falls below the detection limit, reducing the ammonia and amine fingerprints to a  $3 \times 2$  and  $2 \times 3$  pattern, respectively. Figure S4, Supporting Information, provides more details on the dependence of the isotopological patterns on the  $^{1}\mathrm{H} / \mathrm{D}$  ratio in the system. The identity of the equatorial ligands in the complexes is represented by fingerprint III and is again verified by replacing hydrated ammonia and alanine with their  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ - labelled versions (in Figure 4c, ii, iii, respectively). Analogous to what was observed for motifs I and II, the larger chemical shift difference between signals from  $\mathrm{H}$  and  $\mathrm{H}'$  witnessed in motif IV as compared to motif III is attributed to the steric influence of N- bonded alanine in the axial position. The suggested octahedral configurations for motifs III and IV in Figure 4a are presented in Figure 4d, III, IV. These will be crucial for the hyperpolarization of free alanine.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "Motif V (yellow) is highly similar to motif IV (light blue) ..."?
answer: Motif V (yellow) is highly similar to motif IV (light blue) but shifted from the chemical shift region with an N- bonded axial ligand to the region associated with O- bonded axial ligands.
context:
Motif V (yellow) is highly similar to motif IV (light blue) but shifted from the chemical shift region with an N- bonded axial ligand to the region associated with O- bonded axial ligands. Motif V is thus assigned to a complex with ammonia and N- bonded alanine occupying the equatorial ligand positions and O- bonded alanine occupying the axial position (Figure 4d,V). In motif VI (red), the patterns revealing ammonia and N- bonded alanine are mirrored as compared to motif V. As can be seen in Figure 4a, the left side of the motif (H) represents a hydride positioned trans to alanine, while the right side  $(\mathrm{H}^{\prime})$  represents a hydride positioned trans to ammonia. The axial ligand is suggested to be a carboxyl functionality of bidentately ligated alanine also occupying a position in the equatorial plane. This could induce the observed mirroring in the hydride couples. Such bidentate ligation of course renders this configuration not susceptible to SABRE hyperpolarization.

The suggested octahedral configurations for every motif are shown in Figure 4d. Identification of the axial position remains difficult, but the results indisputably demonstrate monodentate ligation of alanine at  $298~\mathrm{K}$  in the presence of ammonia as a co- ligand. This is only the first, yet crucial step toward SABREinduced hyperpolarization of AAs.
evidence_span: Motif V (yellow) is highly similar to motif IV (light blue) but shifted from the chemical shift region with an N- bonded axial ligand to the region associated with O- bonded axial ligands.

Characterization of the  $^{15}N$  resonances was derived from selective  $^{15}N$  decoupling during hydride acquisition. This correlation method directly couples  $^{15}N$  resonances with hyperpolarized hydride signals to which an assignment already is available. a) Hyperpolarized  $^{15}N$  resonances arising from ligated  $^{15}N$ -labelled ammonia in competition with unlabeled alanine. i) Two distinct peak regions around  $\delta -30$  ppm and  $-40$  ppm are observed in congruence with the hydride signal pattern ( $\delta -22.5$  ppm vs  $-23.75$  ppm). answer: Having demonstrated  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  hyperpolarization of ligated ammonia and alanine substrates, hyperpolarization of the free substrates can be attempted.
context:
Having demonstrated  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  hyperpolarization of ligated ammonia and alanine substrates, hyperpolarization of the free substrates can be attempted. The experimental freedom to redistribute hyperpolarization to both ammonia and AA bio- markers inside the spectrometer can itself advance biochemical reaction monitoring, even enabling hyperpolarized multidimensional NMR analysis due to the long inherent  $\mathrm{T}_{1}$  relaxation time of  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  [43,44,63,64,76]

This requires initial hyperpolarization of the ligated substrate in combination with a sufficiently fast chemical exchange of substrate to enable observation of the hyperpolarized  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  nuclei in the free substrates (Figure 6a). To enable observation of free hyperpolarized substrates using SABRE- INEPT, a delay  $(t_{\mathrm{e}})$  must be implemented between the initial transfer of polarization to the ligated substrate and the  $90^{\circ}$  readout pulse (Figure 6b). Hyperpolarized  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  in the free substrate could thus be observable provided the chemical exchange of the substrate is fast enough compared to relaxation in its ligated state.
evidence_span: Having demonstrated  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  hyperpolarization of ligated ammonia and alanine substrates, hyperpolarization of the free substrates can be attempted.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "For hyperpolarization of free substrates, spin- locking- ind..."?
answer: For hyperpolarization of free substrates, spin- locking- induced anticrossings can provide an improved option to transfer spin polarization.[63] When utilizing radiofrequency irradiation to perform spin- locking of ligated substrates, the presence of level anticrossings can be leveraged to facilitate spin polarization transfer at high field throughout the entire spin- lock duration.
context: For hyperpolarization of free substrates, spin- locking- induced anticrossings can provide an improved option to transfer spin polarization.[63] When utilizing radiofrequency irradiation to perform spin- locking of ligated substrates, the presence of level anticrossings can be leveraged to facilitate spin polarization transfer at high field throughout the entire spin- lock duration. This mechanism is related to polarization transfer in low- field SABRE applications, where the polarization transfer occurs without spin- lock. In contrast to SABRE- INEPT, SABRE- SLIC can only be achieved if the  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  chemical shifts of the bound substrates are known.[78] Similar to the approach used for hyperpolarizing  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  nuclei in ligated substrates using SABRE- INEPT, SABRE- SLIC transfer was performed in systems containing either  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ - labelled ammonia (Figure 7a),  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ - labelled ammonia and natural abundance alanine (Figure 7b) or  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ - labelled alanine and natural abundance ammonia (Figure 7c). The spin- locking pulsetrain employed here (Figure S12d, Supporting Information) is specifically designed for singlet- triplet leakage in asymmetric complexes as discussed in Knecht et al.[63] Experimental details, such as the RF- field locking power, irradiation frequency, loop counter, and delay time for exchange to free substrate form can be found in Experimental Section.

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "Performing SABRE at high field allows to fine- tune the flow..."?
answer: Performing SABRE at high field allows to fine- tune the flow of magnetization toward  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ .
context: Performing SABRE at high field allows to fine- tune the flow of magnetization toward  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ . In a system containing  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ - labelled ammonia (dissolved in dusterated methanol via the ammonium buffer solution), a maximal enhancement in  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  of free ammonia surpassing three orders of magnitude (Figure 7a) was achieved. The high efficiency of hyperpolarization observed could originate from the fact that most of the ammonia species are  $\mathrm{ND}_3$ . Relaxation of  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  is therefore suppressed substantially in free form due to the absence of protons with a larger gyromagnetic ratio inducing relaxation. A  $T_1$  of  $71.95 \mathrm{~s}$  was measured for the lifetime of  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  hyperpolarization in free ammonia by fitting an exponential decay onto a series of consecutive  $2^{\circ}$  low- angle pulses separated by a  $5 \mathrm{~s}$  repetition delay (Figure S10, Supporting Information). The main active catalyst configuration present is of course complex (see Figure 4d) since no other co- ligand is used.
evidence_span: Performing SABRE at high field allows to fine- tune the flow of magnetization toward  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ .

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "Access to  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  hyperpolarized free ammonia is..."?
answer: Access to  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  hyperpolarized free ammonia is highly promising since this bio- marker takes a central role in the nitrogen economy of plants as both a growth and nitrogen assimilation source.[3,79,80] Experimental freedom to redistribute hyperpolarization inside the spectrometer to  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  ammonia using the SABRE- SLIC approach can be used for monitoring reaction pathways.
context: Access to  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  hyperpolarized free ammonia is highly promising since this bio- marker takes a central role in the nitrogen economy of plants as both a growth and nitrogen assimilation source.[3,79,80] Experimental freedom to redistribute hyperpolarization inside the spectrometer to  $^{15}\mathrm{N}$  ammonia using the SABRE- SLIC approach can be used for monitoring reaction pathways. Besides circumventing interruptive field- cycling activities, working solely at high- field for hyperpolarization of ammonia in protic solvents provides an additional interesting opportunity. Since the exchangeable protons in ammonia are highly susceptible to protic solvent exchange, hyperpolarization at ultra- low field  $\mu \mathrm{T}$  regimes using  $\mathrm{p - H}_2$  and SABRE catalysts often results in fast redistribution of polarization to the huge number of protons and deuterons present in the system. Zeeman interactions generally distinguishing  $^{15}\mathrm{N}, ^{1}\mathrm{H}$ , and  $^{2}\mathrm{D}$  nuclei are simply negligible at  $\mu \mathrm{T}$  fields generating altogether an efficient hyperpolarization sink.[43,81]

question: According to the passage, what is stated in: "A critical step in these studies was to ensure monodentate l..."?
answer: A critical step in these studies was to ensure monodentate ligation of the amino acid with the iridium spin transfer catalyst.
context: A critical step in these studies was to ensure monodentate ligation of the amino acid with the iridium spin transfer catalyst. Monodentate ligation of alanine on the SABRE active complexes was induced by introducing ammonium hydroxide buffer to deuterated methanol, which progressively produced ammonia as a strong competing ligand. The hydrated ammonium buffer not only enabled monodentate binding in the equatorial plane of the catalyst via the amine functionality of alanine, but the ammonium buffer addition also assisted in the structure elucidation of all catalyst complexes present in the solution. The detailed elucidation used  $^{1}\mathrm{H} / \mathrm{D}$  scrambling caused by the addition of protons to a deuterated solution enabled hydride fingerprinting (i.e., isotopological fingerprinting). 2D- ZQ- NMR gave us then access to the full structural information embedded in the isotopological fingerprints in case spectral overlap in 1D hydride spectra did not give sufficient resolution.
evidence_span: A critical step in these studies was to ensure monodentate ligation of the amino acid with the iridium spin transfer catalyst.

Asymmetric hydrogenation of prochiral olefins has for over 30 years been intensively investigated because of the utility of the chiral products for pharmaceutical and materials applications, to name a few.[1] The majority of catalysts tested have involved rhodium and ruthenium complexes rendered chiral through incorporation of optically active phosphane ligands.[2] Enantioselective olefin hydrogenation with late transition metal catalysts has been, however, essentially limited to specific classes of substrates capable of binding in a bidentate fashion to the metal center, like enamides,[3] unsaturated  $\alpha ,\beta$  carboxylic acids,[4] and allylic and homoallylic alcohols.[5] Much more difficult to reduce with good enantiomeric excesses are olefinic substrates lacking a polar secondary Lewis basic binding group in the correct position. Several groups have tackled the challenging class of di- and trisub

stituted olefins capable of only monodentate coordination to the catalyst metal center with chiral titanium,[6] samarium[7] and late transition metal catalysts[8, 9] and have achieved moderate to excellent enantioselectivities. These results are encouraging, and suggest that new approaches towards the design of catalysts may allow access to a wide range of reaction conditions and efficient metal complexes, extending the generality of enantioselective olefin hydrogenation reactions to broad classes of substrates.

Catalytic results: Applying the optimum conditions found for imine hydrogenation,[12] we examined the reactivity of 1 in the presence of  $0.1\mathrm{M}$  of the hydrocarbon- soluble surfactant AOT (see Scheme 1) and  $0.1\mathrm{M}$  [15]crown- 5 in benzene. AOT is a commercially available surfactant with a sodium sulfonate head group and two branched aliphatic tails that forms reverse micelles in nonpolar solvents.[15] As demonstrated in earlier work, the role of [15]crown- 5 is to complex the sodium cation of AOT, break up reverse micellar aggregates, and promote binding of the bis(2- ethylhexyl)sulfosuccinate anion of AOT to the cationic rhodium catalyst (Scheme 2).[12]

Control experiments were carried out in "regular" solvent systems—neat methanol, benzene, and 1:1 methanol/benzene—at varying temperatures and pressures without additives. The results are summarized in Table 1. Under no conditions were induction periods observed. Hydrogenation of 4 in benzene in the presence of AOT and [15]crown- 5 results in a dramatic increase in enantioselectivity: with AOT and [15]crown- 5, an ee of  $63\%$  (S) can be achieved (run 6), while in "regular" solvents, the highest enantioselectivity observed is  $29\%$  (S) in neat methanol (see runs 1- 4).
